findings.claim: In addGuests.handler.ts, the team permission check uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` where `||` is intended. This reduces it to an owner-only check, so team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.

The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check lowercases the blacklist but compares it against the raw guest email, with no toLowerCase or extractBaseEmail normalization. Blacklisted addresses therefore pass when submitted with different casing or a plus-alias.
De-duplication against existing booking attendees is case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to an existing `a@x.com`.

The server does not de-duplicate the input guests array (uniqueGuests only filters existing attendees and the blacklist). A direct tRPC call with repeated emails creates duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate emails, and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no server-side cap on list size.

The handler passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`. As a result, existing or filtered attendees are classified as new and receive the wrong email (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail), and notifications go to guests who were not actually added.

sendAddGuestsEmails does not check the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata. Emails are therefore sent even when standard host/attendee emails are disabled.
sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect the hideCalendarNotes setting, so hidden notes can be sent to attendees.
`props` is spread after the fixed template props, so callers can override the email's subject, title and header.
New guests are saved with an empty name and inherit the organizer's timeZone/locale, so emails and calendar entries show blank names.

In the add-guests dialog, isInvalidEmail is not reset on success or on overlay/Esc close, so the error state can reappear when the dialog is reopened. Closing via onOpenChange also keeps the old emails, removing all fields makes Add a silent no-op, and the client uniqueness check is case-sensitive.
The invalid-email banner stays visible after the user edits the input to valid values. It clears only on Cancel or on another add attempt.
MultiEmail contains an empty fragment `<></>` in a conditional.
No tests are included for the new addGuests handler/mutation or the new UI components.
The server does not check booking status or time. Guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, which writes attendee rows and sends REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites.
MultiEmail is a near-verbatim copy of the multiemail factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx.
In onError, the toast message is the template string `${code}: ${t(msg)}`, which is never falsy. The unable_to_add_guests fallback is therefore never used, and users see raw 'CODE: key' strings.
The email list state starts as an array containing an empty string rather than an empty array.
evt is built without `team`, so the team-member branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs and team hosts are not notified.
showAttendees is not passed to AttendeeScheduledEmail, so seated events with seatsShowAttendees=true hide the attendee list in these emails.

There is no seated-event handling: attendee rows are created without BookingSeat rows, which bypasses seatsPerTimeSlot. The full attendee list is pushed to the calendar event, and any seat-holder can add guests, exposing seat-holders to each other even when seatsShowAttendees is false.
The new action updates by bookingId only, without seat-level scoping, so on seats events guests are added to the shared booking instead of the current seat.
The booking findFirst include pulls user.credentials (full credential keys), which are never read, and trips @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true.
addGuests uses plain authedProcedure with a custom check instead of bookingsProcedure. Any logged-in attendee can add guests, while COLLECTIVE co-hosts are refused.
About 40 lines of CalendarEvent construction are duplicated from editLocation.handler.ts.
A second prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow refetches the organizer that is already loaded via booking.user.
The email uniqueness check in ZAddGuestsInputSchema is case-sensitive, so User@x.com and user@x.com pass as unique.
The handler throws FORBIDDEN with message key you_do_not_have_permission, which is not defined in en/common.json, so users see the raw key.

There is no transaction or compensation: attendees are written before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped. If it throws, the DB keeps the guests, no emails are sent, and a retry fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid.
MultiEmail uses the array index as the React key, which misbehaves when items are removed from the middle of the list.
MultiEmail.tsx lives inside packages/ui but imports primitives from @calcom/ui, which also exports MultiEmail, creating a circular import risk.
The MultiEmail component reassigns its function parameter `value`.
The MultiEmail component uses the useLocale() hook but lacks the 'use client' directive.
EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials rather than the organizer's. References without a credentialId are matched against the caller's calendars when an attendee or owner adds guests.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
